examples: The house is by the lake.
The dog is by the door.

more.def: Beside or very close to something, or showing who made something.
examples: The small cabin stands by the edge of the forest.
This painting was made by a girl in my class.
We went to school by bus.

easy.def: A word you say when you leave.

more.def: A short, friendly way of saying goodbye.
examples: Bye! I will see you at school on Monday.
Say bye to the ducks before we go.

more.def: Belonging to the past; from long ago.
examples: We read about a bygone age of knights.
The museum showed a bygone era.

easy.def: To go around something instead of through it.

more.def: To go around a place or thing instead of through it.
examples: The new road bypasses the busy downtown streets.
We bypassed the crowd by taking a side door.
The river bypasses the town and flows into a lake.

easy.def: A road that goes around a town.
examples: A bypass goes around the city.

more.def: A road that goes around a town or a busy area instead of through it.
examples: We took the bypass to avoid the heavy traffic downtown.
A new bypass was built to take trucks around the town.
The bypass saved us ten minutes on the trip.

easy.def: A person who watches something happen but is not part of it.

more.def: A person who is present and watches something happen without taking part.
examples: A kind bystander picked up the dropped bag.
